name: Steel City Metal Inc
old_description: Family owned and operated, Steel City Metal Inc. strives to meet the needs of any commercial, residential, and industrial project with honesty and integrity.
about:
Steel City Metal Inc was founded in 1996 in Westover, Alabama, as a family-owned and operated business. The company operates from a facility on Old Highway 280 in Westover, with an administrative office in Birmingham, serving the Greater Birmingham area and surrounding states.

The shop provides welding, fabrication, powder coating, and sandblasting services. Its welders hold AWS certification, and the team brings over 30 years of combined experience in welding and powder coating. Steel City Metal functions as a full-service general contractor for metalwork, handling structural and decorative welding, custom fabrication for homes and businesses, and electrostatic powder coating cured under heat. The company does not sell raw materials but supplies the materials required for each project.

Customers span commercial, industrial, and residential sectors. Projects range from repairs and maintenance for factories and shops to custom builds such as the 15,000-pound "Inception" sculpture installed on the Birmingham walking trail, a collaboration with sister company SuperiorScape. The firm also serves homeowners seeking decorative metalwork and businesses needing code-compliant fabrication.

The company emphasizes integrity, safety, and communication as its differentiators. Leadership cites a team approach rooted in family ownership, with AWS-certified welders prioritizing safety on every job. Steel City Metal says it was built on delivering the cleanest welds and structurally sound structures while maintaining outstanding customer service and attention to detail.

name: Steel Masters NYC
about:
Steel Masters NYC operates from a fabrication shop in Brooklyn, New York. The company was founded in 1972 and remains owner-operated and family-run, carrying more than five decades of continuous service across the New York City metropolitan area.

The shop produces custom steel and iron fabrications for both structural and architectural applications. All items are custom-measured in the field, fabricated in the Brooklyn shop, and installed by the company's own crews.

The customer base spans general contractors, property managers, building owners, facilities managers, architects, engineers, co-op and condo boards, restaurant and retail operators, and homeowners of brownstones, townhouses, and rowhouses. Institutional and commercial clients include hospitals, schools, factories, apartment complexes, and government properties throughout the five boroughs, Long Island, and Westchester.

The company emphasizes that the same organization that welds the steel also installs it, allowing it to hold tolerances and stand behind the finished work. Every project begins with a free estimate based on supplied drawings or photos, followed by a site visit for field measurements, a written proposal, and optional shop drawings for a fee. This hands-on, in-house approach has been the operating model since 1972.

name: Stelray Plastic Products Inc
old_description: A Contract Manufacturer of Precision Injection Molds and Molded Products
about:
Stelray Plastic Products Inc is a family-owned contract manufacturer based in Ansonia, Connecticut. The company has been operating for over 50 years, emphasizing American-made production and a full-service approach to precision injection molding and mold building.

The company operates a 42,000-square-foot facility that houses molding, in-house tool making, quality control, warehousing, secondary operations, and offices. Its molding capacity ranges from 22 to 620 tons, supporting conventional and rotary horizontal injection machines capable of insert molding, overmolding, and multi-material molding. Stelray offers rapid prototyping, design-for-manufacturing reviews, and a suite of post-mold secondary operations including ultrasonic welding, pad printing, heat-staking, soldering, assembly, and packaging. Production volumes span from 100 units to 100 million units annually.

Stelray serves a diverse set of industries: aerospace and automotive, consumer appliance, defense and security, electronics and instrumentation, medical and dental, and water and chemical filtration. The company is FDA registered for medical devices and compliant with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and 21 CFR 820.

Stelray differentiates itself through its family-owned heritage, a full-service in-house tool room, advanced metrology lab with first-article inspection and validation capabilities, and a lean manufacturing philosophy. The company states that its expert engineering staff works with customers to design parts that are both manufacturable and cost-effective from prototype through production.

name: Sterling Furniture Co
old_description: We’re Sterling Furniture Company. Since 1875, we have provided residents of the Wasatch Front a wide range of high quality, customized furniture at accessible prices.
about:
Sterling Furniture Company has operated in Salt Lake City, Utah, since 1875, when master cabinet maker Hans Madsen opened a store on Main Street. The business remains family-owned, now directed by seventh-generation descendants of Madsen, and its flagship location has anchored the Sugar House neighborhood since 1941.

The company retails home furnishings across living room, bedroom, dining room, and office categories, offering customers the ability to customize fabric selections on special orders at no extra charge. It maintains three display floors at its Sugar House showroom and provides delivery throughout the Salt Lake Valley.

Its inventory emphasizes hardwood construction and traditional joinery, with a focus on accessible pricing and flexible payment terms that echo the founder's original installment approach.

The Madsen family frames its differentiation around generational expertise in selecting durable materials and time-honored construction methods, positioning the store as a source for furniture intended to last across generations rather than follow short-lived trends.

name: Stickbulb
old_description: LED fixture manufacturer with showroom, studio, and workshop in a converted iron factory
about:
Founded in 2020, Stickbulb operates a 10,000-square-foot showroom, studio, and workshop inside a converted century-old iron factory in Long Island City, New York. The company is organized as Stickbulb LLC and combines design, prototyping, and production under one roof.

Stickbulb designs and manufactures LED light fixtures using salvaged wood sourced from New York City's urban forest — demolition sites, dismantled water towers, and fallen trees, often within a mile or two of the facility. The product line includes modular collections such as Pillar, Pleat, Skybang, Branching Bough, Ray, Chime, and Diamond, offered in standard sizes with custom lengths and configurations. Production relies on local vendors and flat-pack engineering to minimize shipping volume.

The company serves architects, lighting designers, and interior designers on residential and commercial projects across North America. Notable installations include the Copake Lake House in upstate New York (Desai Chia Architecture), the SoLo House in British Columbia (Perkins & Will), the GL1 project (RUX Studios), and 100 Norfolk in Manhattan (ODA). Stickbulb also supplies trade professionals through showrooms and agents.

Stickbulb positions its differentiation around climate-conscious manufacturing. It has been Climate Neutral certified since 2020, tracking, reducing, and offsetting emissions, and became a Certified B Corporation in 2022. The hyper-local supply chain diverts old-growth timber from landfills, while modular flat-pack designs lower the carbon footprint of distribution.

name: Sticks, Inc.
old_description: Sticks Handmade pieces are all one-of-a-kind and created by artisan hands from start to finish. Art & furniture made in America since 1992.
about:
Sticks, Inc. was founded in 1992 in West Des Moines, Iowa. The company began as a studio creating one-of-a-kind handmade art and furniture, with each piece drawn, wood-burned, and painted by artisan hands.

Today Sticks operates a production studio in Des Moines where it manufactures a wide range of home furnishings and accessories, including sculptures, wall plaques, lamps, lazy Susans, furniture such as tables, chairs, beds, and case goods, as well as holiday ornaments and custom heirloom pieces. The process remains entirely handcrafted: designs are hand-drawn, wood-burned, and hand-painted. The company also runs the Sticks Gallery in Des Moines’ Historic East Village, a retail destination opened in 2002 that carries the full Sticks line alongside work from over 150 other American makers.

Sticks serves both direct consumers and the trade. Collections span bedroom, dining, entryway, kitchen, living room, and office categories, with themed lines such as Americana, Lake, Mountain, Wine, and Wedding/Anniversary.

The company’s stated distinction is its commitment to storytelling through art: every piece is created from start to finish by artisans in the Des Moines studio, and the custom program lets customers commission furniture and accessories inspired by personal stories, places, or family history. This emphasis on narrative-driven, American-made craftsmanship has defined the brand since its inception.

name: Stixon Labels
old_description: Stixon Labels is a manufacturer of custom pressure sensitive labels. We produce labels up to 13.75" x 15" in as many...
about:
Stixon Labels operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it was established in 1991 by founder Robert W. Chavez. The business traces its roots to 1955 when Chavez began designing and selling labels, adding flexible packaging in 1961 and forming New Mexico Plastics in 1985. Today the company is owned by Chavez’s daughters—Beverly, Julie, Barbara, and Cristina—who grew up in the label manufacturing business and now lead it as a family-owned operation.

The company manufactures custom pressure-sensitive labels and flexible packaging using flexographic printing, producing labels up to 13.75 by 15 inches. It also provides design and artwork services through a computerized art department, foil stamping, and thermal-transfer blank labels. The staff includes press operators with tenures exceeding 30 years, and most employees have been with the company for more than 15 years.

Stixon serves wineries, distilleries, food and beverage producers, and personal-care brands. Its client list includes Gruet Winery and St. Clair Winery in New Mexico, Headframe Spirits in Montana, Dion’s Pizza Salad Dressings, 505 Southwestern Chile & Salsa, El Pinto Chile & Salsa, New Mexico Piñon Coffee, Sombra Professional Therapy Products, and Marble Brewery, along with retail packaging such as foil-stamped shopping bags.

The company emphasizes service as its differentiator, offering creative, cost-effective solutions from design to finished product. Its long-tenured team and family ownership are cited as reasons for consistent quality and responsiveness.

name: StockPKG Films
old_description: Nationally stocked film substrates. Innovative laminations. Large U.S. inventory selection. Sustainable solutions. Educated sales professionals. Industry leading pricing. Dependable products.
about:
StockPKG Films, headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, was founded in 2008. The company began as a supplier of packaging films and has since expanded to offer custom lamination and precision slitting services from its own facilities.

The company produces and stocks a range of flexible packaging films including barrier, non-barrier, and metalized substrates, as well as proprietary pre-laminated Lightning Lam films featuring InkRite Technology for up to 99% ink adhesion. It also manufactures LidShield lidding films with options such as anti-fog, breathable perforations, and enhanced barrier constructions. In-house capabilities include precision slitting and rewinding to customer-specified widths, along with custom lamination. StockPKG operates a Make & Hold program that allows customers to lock in pricing and maintain inventory across multiple U.S. warehouses.

StockPKG serves printers and converters in the flexible packaging industry, with a focus on food packaging applications. Its clear BOPP films are stocked for common food packaging needs, while its Lightning Lam line addresses ink adhesion challenges in digital printing. Customers include businesses seeking quick lead times and consistent quality for both standard and custom film constructions.

The company differentiates itself through its InkRite Technology, which reduces ink consumption and improves print quality on laminated surfaces, and through its Make & Hold inventory strategy that helps mitigate raw-material price fluctuations. A team of sales representatives with decades of industry experience supports product selection and technical requirements.

The company serves the Foodservice, Food Ingredients, and Retail Private Label markets in North America.

about:
Subsalve USA is based in North Kingstown, Rhode Island, and was founded in 1977 by Richard Fryburg. The company began as a specialist in engineered inflatables for marine and military applications, and in 2017 it became part of Performance Inflatables Co LLC.

The company designs and manufactures a range of engineered inflatables, including underwater lift bags, inflation hose assemblies, station manifolds, inflation yoke assemblies, and acoustic and remote tablet actuation systems. It maintains an inventory of standard products and offers custom design services for specialized applications.

Subsalve serves industries such as aircraft recovery, ship and boat salvage, marine construction, offshore oilfield diving, explosive ordnance disposal, pipeline and tunnel construction, proofload testing, public safety, research, and shipyard operations. Its customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, all branches of the U.S. Armed Forces, NASA, the FBI, private-sector companies, and governments of more than 30 foreign countries.

The company differentiates itself by using polyurethane-coated fabrics—nylon, polyester, and Kevlar—in all its lift bags, which it says provides superior puncture, abrasion, and chemical resistance. All products are made in the USA, tested before shipping, and carry a one-year warranty. Subsalve holds compliance with IMCA D-016-AIRBAGS, ABS, and U.S. Department of Defense standards, and holds multiple patents for its designs.

about:
Summit Interconnect's Chicago facility operates from Schaumburg, Illinois, as part of a North American network founded in 2016 when KCA Electronics in Anaheim and Marcel Electronics International in Orange were acquired to form the company. The Chicago site was added in 2021 through the Eagle Electronics acquisition, which brought quick-turn commercial prototype capabilities. Leadership includes President & CEO Shane Whiteside and a team of veterans paired with younger professionals across engineering, manufacturing, and quality roles.

The company fabricates complex rigid, RF/microwave, rigid-flex, and flex printed circuit boards, and provides full turnkey prototype assembly. Across seven connected high-tech facilities and eight North American locations, Summit runs 1,250-plus employees producing boards from two layers to 30-plus layers standard, with emerging capability beyond 44 layers. Panel sizes reach 24 by 36 inches; HDI sequential lamination goes to seven layers. Processes include laser microvias, blind/buried vias, via-in-pad with conductive or non-conductive fill, and surface finishes such as ENIG, ENEPIG, immersion silver, and OSP. Assembly handles fine-pitch placement to 0.04 mils, components down to 01005, BGA reball, underfill, conformal coating, box build, and functional test.

Summit positions itself as one of the largest PCB manufacturers in North America, differentiating through redundant facilities, field application engineers across the continent, and a one-stop model that combines fabrication, assembly, and test under AS9100D, NADCAP, ITAR, and IPC Class III certifications. The stated mission is to help customers succeed while building a workplace where the team can thrive.

Sunlight Solar emphasizes its local roots as a differentiator, stating that deep knowledge of regional permitting, utility requirements, and climate conditions allows it to build systems that perform reliably over decades. SunMED Medical Solutions was founded in 2002 in Marlton, New Jersey, as a provider of advanced in-home medical equipment and superior patient support. The company, led by President Bill Lobosco, began with a focus on delivering specialized equipment directly to patients' homes while managing the complex insurance claims process.

Today SunMED operates nationwide as a diversified durable medical equipment (DME) provider and claims specialist. Its service lines include lymphedema therapy support, wound care therapy (covering negative-pressure wound therapy and compression wound care), women's health (post-surgical garments and new-mother support), and a Supplier National Access Program (S.N.A.P.) that helps medical suppliers establish a national footprint. The company also administers the Wellcare for Women group benefit for employers. SunMED's support staff functions as product and claims subject-matter experts rather than order takers, handling insurance verification, benefit maximization, and patient guidance.

The company serves patients, referring clinicians, therapists, medical suppliers, and employers across the home healthcare, wound care, lymphedema management, and women's health markets. Clinicians rely on SunMED to deliver prescribed products and navigate reimbursement, while suppliers use the S.N.A.P. platform to access national distribution. Employers adopt Wellcare for Women as a voluntary benefit.

SunMED differentiates itself by maintaining a live, telephone-based support team at a time when many competitors have shifted to online-only administration. The firm states that its core purpose is "next-level service," emphasizing personal interaction and claims expertise to capture every eligible health coverage benefit for patients.

The company processes locally sourced trees that might otherwise be wasted, turning urban wood into high-quality lumber and slabs while emphasizing heritage and sustainability.

The company provides custom mobile and stationary sawmilling for logs up to 60 inches in diameter, vacuum kiln drying to a target moisture content of 6–8 percent, wood sanitization, and sales of premium native hardwood lumber. Services are offered both at its Tupelo facility and on-site for customers across Lee County and North Mississippi.

Superior Artisan Wood serves woodworkers, contractors, arborists, homeowners, designers, and municipalities. Builders, furniture makers, and DIY enthusiasts purchase its rotating selection of kiln-dried hardwoods, while the log donation program allows community members to give fallen trees a second life.

The business emphasizes sustainability, aiming to reduce landfill waste and carbon emissions by preserving urban trees. It markets itself as the only certified urban wood producer in Mississippi, highlighting a commitment to heritage and environmental impact.

about:
Switchback Medical is based in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota. The company was co-founded by Brady Hatcher, who serves as CEO, and Randy Beyreis, who serves as CTO. The leadership team also includes Jim Moran as COO, Jesse Jensen as VP of Global Integration and Quality, and several other vice presidents overseeing operations, quality, and business development.

The company provides contract design and manufacturing services for medical devices, offering a single-source solution from concept through commercialization. Its capabilities include injection molding, balloon forming, nitinol shape setting, thermal bonding (laser, RF, and heated die), braiding, coiling, laser welding, 3D printing, and sterile packaging. Operations are housed in a 120,000-square-foot facility that includes approximately 13,500 square feet of ISO Class 7 cleanroom space, an ISO Class 8 silicone processing room, an on-site machine shop, and a design assurance lab equipped for tensile, leak, burst, and simulated-use testing.

Switchback Medical serves the medical device industry, working with customers who need design verification, process development, and commercial-scale manufacturing of catheter-based and other interventional devices. The company’s external partners include suppliers for ethylene oxide sterilization, laser processing, extrusion, and hydrophilic coating.

The company states its mission is to partner with customers to develop and commercialize medical devices with unmatched speed, responsiveness, and ingenuity. It emphasizes a single-source model intended to reduce development costs and time to market, backed by ISO 13485 certification, FDA registration, and ISO 14971:2019 risk management practices.

about:
Sypris Electronics LLC operates from Tampa, Florida, drawing on over 60 years of experience in electronic manufacturing. The company traces its roots to a heritage of building mission-critical electronic and electro-mechanical systems, and in August 2016 it divested its Cyber Security Services and Product business to Analog Devices to focus exclusively on manufacturing and engineering services.

The firm specializes in high-mix, low-to-medium volume production of circuit card assemblies (CCAs), modules, and complex box builds. Its process capabilities include conformal coating, potting, underfills, polymeric staking, environmental stress screening (ESS), and design-for-excellence (DFx) services. Engineering support spans new product introduction (NPI), prototyping, limited-rate initial production (LRIP), and full-rate production, all managed through a Lean Six Sigma framework that emphasizes risk mitigation, traceability, and change management.

Sypris serves military and defense (DoD), space (both government and commercial), undersea (telecommunications, oil and gas, scientific), civil avionics, telecommunications, and industrial markets. Its customer base includes tier-one primes such as L3Harris, Collins Aerospace, and Lockheed Martin, as well as a Fortune 100 global security and defense company.

The company differentiates itself through a secure, COMSEC- and AS9100-certified facility, a culture of continuous improvement branded as the Sypris Enterprise System, and a commitment to counterfeit mitigation, component engineering, and life-cycle sustainment services such as spares and repairs.

TMF serves customers needing complete product development and manufacturing solutions, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals. The sheet metal fabrication business has progressed from the early days of using hand tools into a modern facility of sheet metal manufacturing equipment including: a laser running at the speed of light, robotic arc welding.
about:
Tampa Sheet Metal Company was founded in 1920 by John Jiretz Sr., a craftsman who learned his trade in Austria and Germany. The company is located in Tampa, Florida, and remains family-owned, currently managed by John L. Jiretz (president, grandson of the founder) and John D. Jiretz (great-grandson). It began as a sheet metal fabrication business using hand tools and has evolved into a modern facility.

The company provides full-service sheet metal fabrication from design to finished product. Processes include laser cutting (4,000-watt laser cutting stainless steel, steel, aluminum, brass, copper on a 60x120-inch table), CNC turret punching (36-station, 45-ton press), press braking (12-foot and 6-foot capacity), metal shearing (12-foot, quarter-inch thick steel), robotic welding (steel, aluminum, stainless steel), hardware insertion, countersinking, counterboring, and mechanical assembly. The facility spans 25,000 square feet near downtown Tampa.

Tampa Sheet Metal serves industrial, commercial, and construction sectors. Project examples from the company's archive include industrial facilities, shopping malls, high-rise buildings, EPC projects, infrastructure, and commercial buildings.

The company emphasizes its long-standing dedication to quality and service since 1920, with a quality control program certified by FM Approvals and Keystone Certifications. It also highlights environmental responsibility, noting that sheet metal is 100% recyclable and all scrap is melted down for reuse.

about:
Tangent Cable Systems Inc operates from Wilmington, Delaware. The company's founding year is not publicly disclosed, and ownership details are not specified. The firm provides commercial cabling and wiring services through IBEW-trained electrical craftsmen. Its scope covers electrical design and project management, ongoing maintenance, structured network cabling installation, and security system deployment including card access, CCTV, control cabinet wiring, conduit raceway, and intercom systems. The company also handles sign and pole light service. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

Tangent serves financial institutions, military installations, the Delaware gaming industry, communications companies, and general service-industry clients. It collaborates with architects, designers, IT professionals, facility managers, construction managers, and security engineers to ensure compliant, adequate cabling infrastructure.

The company emphasizes its Delaware State Alarm license, which requires FBI background checks on core employees, providing a vetted workforce for sensitive environments. Clients cite commitment, workmanship, and turnaround time as distinguishing factors, with long-term relationships spanning over a decade.

name: Tarrier Foods Corporation
old_description: However, Ann quickly realized she had bigger ambitions and decided to take control of her own destiny. With determination and a trusted partner by her side, she stepped out and founded her own business - focused on mixing nuts and dried fruits.
about:
Tarrier Foods Corporation operates from Columbus, Ohio, as a family-owned food processor founded by Ann, who left a previous role to start her own business blending nuts and dried fruits. The company does not disclose a founding year, but describes decades of expertise in the ingredient space.

The company processes, blends, and packages sweet and savory inclusions and toppings for branded, private-label, and retail products. Its capabilities include simultaneous multi-item blending, size reduction, roasting, seasoning, and a range of packaging formats such as portion-control pouches, stand-up pouches, pillow pouches, bulk bag-in-box, bowls, and shakers. Tarrier also maintains a stocked inventory of branded inclusions—including OREO®, Chips Ahoy!®, Nutter Butter®, and Sour Patch Kids® Bitz—available for immediate shipment through distributor Dot Foods.

Tarrier serves food manufacturers, quick-service restaurant chains, distributors, and private-label brands across the United States and Canada. Its ingredients appear in desserts, baked goods, salads, and sandwiches. Long-term customers cite relationships spanning 11 to 20 years, highlighting the company’s role as an innovation partner for product development.

Tarrier emphasizes speed to market, custom formulation flexibility, and rigorous food safety controls as its differentiators. The founder’s original vision—to control her own destiny by creating unique ingredient blends—remains central to the company’s pitch: helping brands move faster from concept to production with tailored ingredient solutions.

The business curates and sells a range of shelf-stable products from New Mexican brands such as Santa Fe Seasons, Rio Grande Roasters, and Santa Fe Gourmet. Offerings include Hatch chile salsas and sauces, piñon coffee, biscochitos, popcorn, soup mixes, and gift bundles. Taste New Mexico emphasizes its NM True Certified and Certified Hatch Chile Food Vendor designations as marks of authenticity. It promotes family recipes passed down through generations and guarantees that all products are traditionally made in New Mexico.

name: Taurus Engineering And Manufacturing
old_description: Flexibility and rapid responsiveness is what makes Taurus Engineering a valuable partner for medical product developers.
about:
Taurus Engineering and Manufacturing operates from a 33,000-square-foot facility in St. Paul, Minnesota. The company traces its roots to 2008, when John Philipsen acquired Innovative Mold and rebranded it as Taurus Engineering.

The firm specializes in precision injection molded components, complex subassemblies, and fully packaged assemblies for medical devices. Its capabilities include insert molding, over-molding with thermoplastic elastomers, and Class 7 cleanroom molding. The plant runs 20 injection molding machines ranging from 28 to 350 tons on a 24/5 schedule, and it maintains in-house toolmaking for single- and multi-cavity molds. Secondary operations, assembly, packaging, and supply chain management are offered under a complete contract manufacturing model.

Taurus serves medical product developers and OEMs, producing parts such as connectors, infusion sets, IV catheters, valve swivels, and heat-and-moisture exchangers. Customers range from early-stage startups needing rapid prototypes to established manufacturers requiring high-volume production and tool transfers.

The company emphasizes a "Thinking Outside the Box" philosophy, positioning itself as a strategic partner rather than a vendor. It highlights flexibility, rapid responsiveness, and a design-for-manufacturing approach to accelerate time to market and reduce costs. Its quality system is ISO 13485 certified by Intertek and FDA registered, supported by first-article inspections, IQ/OQ/PQ validations, PPAPs, and statistical process controls.

Team Apparel & Specialties operates from Green Bay, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1984 by Chris and Gail Docky as a part-time venture that quickly moved to a storefront on Western Avenue. The business remained locally owned and, in April 2008, was purchased by top salesman Travis Herber, who continues as president.

The company provides custom decoration services including screen printing, embroidery, graphic design, CAD printing/wax transfer, and promotional product sourcing. All production is done in-house at a custom facility built in 1993, which houses the largest showroom in the Green Bay area. The shop handles orders ranging from small runs to large volumes for uniforms, team apparel, and branded merchandise.

Clients include schools such as UW‑Green Bay athletics, religious organizations like Life Church, corporate accounts including Packerland Brokerage Services, American‑3 Fab, and JBS, as well as numerous local sports programs and community groups. The company also operates online stores and order-form systems for organizations that want to manage apparel purchasing without inventory.

Team Apparel emphasizes that its 35‑plus years of success stem from long‑term relationships built on trust, fast turnaround enabled by in‑house production, and a mission to deliver the right product at a fair price with reliable service.

name: Team JDC - Gonzales, Louisiana
old_description: With over 50 years in the service, parts, and rental business, JDC (Jack Doheny Company) has expanded to provide sewer, industrial, underground, and electric utility solutions to municipalities and customers from coast to coast in the United States and Canada.
about:
Jack Doheny Company (JDC), based in Gonzales, Louisiana, has spent more than five decades in the service, parts, and rental business. The company expanded from its roots to provide sewer, industrial, underground, and electric utility solutions to municipalities and customers across the United States and Canada.

JDC operates 18 locations coast to coast, offering equipment rentals, pre-owned equipment sales, pipeline inspection, parts distribution, and full-service repair. Its in-house technician team handles vacuum systems, pumps, blowers, fans, chassis, hydraulic systems, hoses, water tanks, and cyclones. The company stocks over 300,000 parts, tools, and accessories from brands such as Warthog, Vyper, Spartan, Piranha, Helix, T&T Tools, Dica, Elliott, Vivax, and Skylift. A partnership with Huber adds combination sewer cleaners to the lineup. Rental equipment is kept on-site for immediate deployment, and free 360° inspections are available to assess equipment health.

The customer base includes municipalities, electric utilities, construction firms, and contractors specializing in sewer cleaning, pipeline maintenance, and infrastructure projects. Examples range from a city purchasing a street sweeper to a utility company specifying a digger derrick. JDC also provides operator training and technical support, with testimonials citing on-site training for combination sewer cleaner crews and continuing-education credits.

JDC emphasizes safety, reliability, and rapid response. Its differentiators include a national footprint with local stock, a large ready-to-ship parts inventory, certified technicians, and the Huber partnership for engineered combo-truck solutions. The company positions itself as a single-source partner for infrastructure equipment needs.

about:
Tech Electronics of Kansas City operates from Lenexa, Kansas, and has served the Midwest since its founding in 1963. The company provides building technology services across the Kansas City metropolitan area, including Jackson County, Clay County, and surrounding communities such as Independence, Overland Park, Blue Springs, and Olathe.

The firm designs, installs, and maintains fire and life safety systems (fire detection, suppression, mass notification, public safety DAS), security solutions (video surveillance, access control, intrusion detection, visitor management), and communication and AV technologies (intercom, voice, audio visual, nurse call, wireless clocks). It also offers ongoing building technology services including fire and security monitoring, inspections, testing, wireless assessments, and a Technology as a Service model. The company references a featured project, "Project SuperBowl," which deployed a public safety DAS for a 1.1 million-square-foot fulfillment center in Kansas City, Kansas.

Tech Electronics serves commercial, construction, education, government, healthcare, industrial, and stadium sectors. Notable clients include the University of Kansas Hospital, the University of Missouri–Kansas City, Kansas City International Airport, the T‑Mobile Center, and the Colorado School of Mines.

The company emphasizes its decades of industry knowledge, tailored solutions for each facility, and a Technology as a Service approach that reduces operating costs while providing access to the latest systems.

name: Technical Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: – the trusted contract electronics manufacturer of choice to the
about:
Founded in 1985 in Durham, Connecticut, Technical Manufacturing Corporation (TMC) has operated as a contract electronics manufacturer for four decades.

TMC specializes in the assembly of advanced printed circuit boards for the domestic aerospace and defense industry, delivering high-reliability products where operation and continued performance are critical. Its service portfolio spans printed circuit board assembly for prototype and production volumes, wire and cable assembly, system integration, and a suite of quality programs including FOD control, ESD control, MSL management, counterfeit parts mitigation, cleanliness testing, and conflict minerals reporting. The facility houses a Fischer XDL high-performance energy dispersive X-ray fluorescence (EDXRF) measuring instrument for material verification.

The company serves the aerospace and defense sector across both commercial and government programs. Its assemblies are used in intelligence, surveillance & reconnaissance (ISR) systems, satellite and space flight vehicles, troop and personnel support equipment, aircraft and missile platforms, and undersea and surface warships. Customers include prime contractors and subcontractors within the U.S. Defense Industrial Base.

TMC emphasizes a safety-first manufacturing philosophy, stating that on-time delivery and competitive pricing alone are insufficient for mission-critical applications. Differentiators cited include Nadcap AC7120 accreditation for printed board and circuit card assemblies, ITAR registration, CMMC 2.0 Level 2 cybersecurity compliance, and membership in the Aerospace Components Manufacturers (ACM) Group.

In 1987, Tecnova Electronics, Inc. was established to combine design and contract manufacturing under one roof, creating a single-source solution for electronics production. The business remains led by the Coleman family, with Terry Coleman Sr. as CEO of Tecnova, Inc. and Terence Coleman Jr. as President of the Electronics division.

The company provides comprehensive electronic manufacturing services, specializing in printed circuit board assembly (SMT and through-hole), electro-mechanical assembly, box builds, cable and wire harness assembly, and inspection and testing including in-house X-ray and automated optical inspection (AOI). Its ISO 9001:2015-certified facility operates multiple high-speed SMT production lines with high-accuracy pick-and-place systems, and offers conformal coating with silicone and acrylic materials. Tecnova handles odd-formed parts such as large connectors and Pem-nuts, and supports production volumes from prototype through mid-volume to large-scale runs. Additional capabilities include product development services such as electronic prototyping, motor drive development, power electronics design, and project management.

Tecnova serves mid-sized original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) across industrial electronics sectors, including industrial sensing, monitoring, and controls, motor drive systems, and power electronics. The company maintains partnerships as an Analog Devices Design Partner and a member of the Hirose Solution Partner Network, indicating engagement with component suppliers and technology ecosystems. Customers typically seek a seamless integration of design and manufacturing to avoid finger-pointing between separate vendors.

Tecnova differentiates itself through its "design-it-right, build-it-right" philosophy, embedding quality at every stage rather than relying solely on end-of-line inspection. The firm has been recognized multiple times as a Quality Leadership 100 company by Quality Magazine, including the #1 ranking in 2024. By offering both engineering design and contract manufacturing under common ownership, Tecnova aims to provide accountability and smoother project outcomes for clients.

about:
The Brickle Group is headquartered in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, where it began as a third‑generation family business founded by Hyman Brickle in 1937. After working for a local rag merchant, Hyman launched H. Brickle & Son, Inc. to trade recycled fibers between textile mills, becoming the first woolen waste dealer in the South and establishing a foundation built on material recovery.

Today the group operates six divisions. Bouckaert Industrial Textiles custom‑engineers needle‑punch nonwoven felts. Northwest Woolen Mills has produced wool and synthetic blankets for 68 years, supplying army blankets and emergency‑relief blankets for humanitarian crises worldwide. H. Brickle Fiber Trading & Recycling purchases mill waste, recycles it, and spins woolen yarns (including 2‑ to 4‑ply constructions) for other textile manufacturers. F&M Dyeing Corp provides commercial‑quality dyeing and fulling for wool and fur felt hat bodies. Brickle Realty Group manages and develops industrial and commercial properties, while Heat Smart assembles energy‑assistance kits — wool blankets, weatherstripping, and conservation tips — for low‑income households.

Customers span textile mills, hat manufacturers, government agencies (including the U.S. Department of Energy), disaster‑relief organizations, and senior‑energy programs. The group's blankets have been deployed in natural disasters and political conflicts globally, and its fiber‑recycling services feed raw material back into the textile supply chain.

The company credits its longevity to diversification — acquiring Northwest Woolen Mills in 1978 and Bouckaert Industrial Textiles in 2000 — and to a mission of developing tailored products while maintaining a culture rooted in family, quality of life, and performance.

about:
The Colorado Tent Company operates from Denver, Colorado, tracing its roots to 1890 when the Denver Tent and Awning Company opened on Larimer Street to serve miners, ranchers, railroad crews, and military posts. A second shop, the Colorado Tent & Awning Company, was founded by Robert S. Gutshall in 1899 on Lawrence Street. The two competitors merged in 2003, and in 2022 the business was acquired by Harlan and Karah Hummer, who retained the existing team and standards.

The company handcrafts canvas wall tents, tipis, awnings, and custom shelter goods at its facility at 10975 E. 55th Avenue. Every tent is cut, sewn, and inspected by hand using 10.10‑oz Sunforger® marine‑grade cotton duck, double‑stitched seams, and brass hardware. Production runs are limited each month, with a current lead time of three to six weeks for both stock and custom orders.

Customers span hunting outfitters, camps and non‑profits, glamping and hospitality operators, event and gathering planners, and commercial and corporate clients. Historical contracts include military, scouting, and ranching accounts.

The shop differentiates itself through a lifetime warranty against manufacturing defects, a repair‑first design philosophy (no glues or seals that prevent future fixes), and adherence to the same materials and methods used since the early 1900s.

about:
The Little Potato Company is headquartered in DeForest, Wisconsin. The company traces its roots to 1996 when Angela and her father started with two shovels, a rented one-acre plot, and a dream in Canada. Canadian owned and operated since 1996, the business expanded to the United States in 2016, establishing American operations in Wisconsin. The company partners with family farms such as Coloma Farms, which has been operating since 1961, and growers like Steve who joined his family farm after college and has supplied the company since 2016.

The company specializes in growing, processing, packaging, and distributing small potato varieties. Working with a network of family farms across Canada and the U.S., it oversees planning, planting, growing, harvesting, and storing practices through its variety development team. The potatoes are packaged into consumer-ready products, including microwave-ready flavored lines such as Savory Herb and garlic and herb, and distributed to retail stores.

Its customers include busy families seeking convenient, fresh whole-food options, as evidenced by consumer testimonials. The company also partners with retail and office partners for distribution.

The business was built around family values—integrity, reliability, respect, and humility—and aims to create "little moments of happiness" for consumers. Sustainability is a core belief, reflected in responsible farmland use and generational partnerships with farming families.

old_description: We are a family-run, privately-owned, U.S. Corporation processing fresh-packed
about:
The Neil Jones Food Company is a family-run, privately-owned U.S. corporation headquartered in Vancouver, Washington. Founded in 1915 as San Benito Foods, the company began with a single can of premium San Benito tomatoes processed fresh from the field. The business has remained under family stewardship, with James Matthew Jones currently serving as CEO.

The company processes fresh-packed Pacific Northwest fruit — including pears, cherries, plums, and cranberries — and California tomato products such as canned tomatoes, pouches, custom sauces, and industrial varieties. It operates three processing facilities strategically located for national and international shipping. The Northwest Packing facility has canned Pacific Northwest fruit and produced industrial juices, purees, and blends since the 1970s. The TomaTek facility, built in the 1980s, specializes in aseptic technology for fresh-pack California tomatoes in industrial sizes and #10 equivalent pouches. All products are made in the U.S.A.

Customers span foodservice, industrial, retail, chain, and international channels. The company serves independent restaurants, school lunch programs, food manufacturers, chain restaurants, healthcare facilities, juice manufacturers, and cruise lines worldwide. Products appear under private label brands and in restaurants across the country.

The company emphasizes sustainable fresh-packing within hours of harvest, working closely with growers and agronomists to ensure quality ingredients. It highlights its commitment to not taking shortcuts, maintaining strict quality standards, and offering extensive customization capabilities for private label and foodservice partners.

old_description: Helping Kansas, Missouri, and Iowa families save on energy since 2014.
about:
The Solar Guys was founded in 2014 in Ankeny, Iowa, by brothers Jesse and Jereme. The Iowa-raised, family-owned company began with a mission to make clean energy simple for customers across Kansas, Missouri, and Iowa.

The company designs and installs custom solar energy systems for residential and commercial properties, along with battery backup and service for existing arrays. All work is performed in-house — from site assessment and system engineering through permitting, installation, and ongoing monitoring — without subcontractors. They evaluate roof condition, structure energy-use data, and size each system to the property’s long-term performance. A 25-year workmanship warranty covers every installation.

The Solar Guys serves homeowners and commercial property owners in Kansas, Missouri, and Iowa. Residential clients receive custom rooftop systems sized to actual usage, while commercial projects are engineered for 10-, 20-, and 25-year returns, with assistance navigating tax credits, depreciation, and C-PACE financing. The team also services and repairs systems it did not originally install.

The brothers started the business to offer honest pricing, real-person communication, and installations built to outlast the warranty. Their differentiators include a fully in-house crew, no-subcontractor policy, custom design for every roof and budget, and a commitment to handle all permitting and utility paperwork.

A multidisciplinary staff of mechanics, engineers, electricians, programmers, and machinists supports design, fabrication, and service.

TEC serves manufacturers in the wire and cable, fiber optic, and plastics extrusion sectors. Its equipment is used in the production of insulated wire, fiber optic cable, plastic tubing, profile shapes, and compounded materials. The company provides both complete production lines and individual machines to integrate into existing operations.

TEC differentiates itself by starting with a base machine platform and customizing it to each customer's unique requirements. The company emphasizes its experienced in-house team and its ability to deliver end-to-end solutions for fiber optic cable products, as well as its commitment to building dependable machines for the wire and cable production process.

about:
Three R Plastics Inc. operates from Spring Grove, Illinois, where it was founded in 1994. Three generations of the founding family work together in the business, which has grown steadily since its start.

The company combines injection molding and mold making under one roof, running a full-service mold manufacturing shop in-house. Nearly all of the molds it builds — about 99 percent — are run in its own molding department. It also accepts transfer molds and provides mold servicing for customers who lack that capability. Its precision injection molding covers parts from smaller than a fingernail up to several pounds, using a wide range of resins including glass- and carbon-filled grades and high-temperature materials such as PEEK and Ultem. Swiss lathes are used for custom production pieces and to supplement molding with overmolded materials.

The company serves a wide range of markets, though specific industries are not detailed in its public materials.

What distinguishes the operation is the integration of mold building and molding in a single facility, allowing tight control from tool design through production. The ability to take on transfer molds and service existing tooling extends that control to projects that originated elsewhere.

about:
Timbercraft Custom Dovetail Drawers was founded in 2003 in New Milford, Connecticut. The company began by specializing in custom dovetail drawers for cabinetmakers, millworkers, and contractors throughout the Northeast.

The company operates a lean manufacturing facility that produces custom dovetail drawers with a consistent 3-5 day turnaround. Drawers are made from select or better grades of maple and birch, with 5/8-inch side thickness, 1/16-inch radius top edges, and 3/8-inch Baltic birch bottoms. A 100% solid UV coating provides a hard, uniform, solvent-free finish. Heights range from 2 1/8 inches to 12 1/8 inches for birch and 11 3/8 inches for maple, with edge-glue panel techniques allowing heights up to 22 3/8 inches. Widths and depths run from 3 inches to 58 inches for birch and 43 3/4 inches for maple.

Timbercraft serves cabinetmakers, millworkers, and general contractors across the Northeast, including the Tri-State area where palletized orders ship next business day via LTL. The company does not offer value, budget, or economy grade drawers, emphasizing premium materials and refusing to recover scrap wood for drawer components.

The company highlights its consistent 3-5 day turnaround, unmatched customer service, and premium material selection as key differentiators. Orders are acknowledged by email and, once approved and released into production, cannot be changed. Credit cards are kept on file and charged the day before completion, and all freight charges are prepaid and included in acknowledgments.

about:
Todd's Warehouse (operating as Todd's Foods) traces its roots to 1926 when Martin Todd and his wife Arlene began selling seasoning blends to meat lockers and markets in Des Moines, Iowa. The company expanded across the Midwest through a network of sales routes. In June 2011, Andy Holt acquired Todd's LTD, and in October 2015 the business purchased the Summit Foods factory in Madison, Nebraska, adding liquid blending and packaging capacity. Today the company operates dry production facilities in Des Moines at the intersection of I-80 and I-235 and a liquid production plant in Madison, NE, positioning it for national distribution.

The company provides contract food manufacturing (co-packing), dry bulk blending, dry packaging, and liquid packaging services. Its liquid lines handle hot-fill products such as BBQ sauces, salsas, salad dressings, and vinegars in containers ranging from 10-ounce jars to large totes, and employ ozone sanitation for bottles and headspace. Dry capabilities include flexible stand-up pouches and various bulk, restaurant, and retail pack formats. A HACCP program and SQF certification govern food safety, while a Process Authority oversees acidified food processes. The firm also offers formulation development for kosher, organic, non-irradiated, GMO-free, and gluten-free requirements.

Customers include large commercial food manufacturers, restaurant chains, grocery delis, foodservice operators, retail brands, hospitals, and institutional buyers. Todd's has helped entrepreneurs turn home recipes into commercial products sold on retail, hospital, restaurant, and institutional shelves. The company emphasizes customized production for medium to large orders and serves both established companies and start-ups.

Todd's differentiates itself through its SQF certification, ozone sanitation, hot-fill and acidified process capabilities, and strategic Midwest locations that enable cost-effective shipping nationwide. The business highlights its 90-plus years of experience in seasonings and spices, award-winning products, and a focus on being a reliable partner for food packaging needs.

about:
Tokyo Ohka Kogyo America Inc. (TOK America) operates from Hillsboro, Oregon, as the U.S. supply hub for its Japanese parent, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo Co., Ltd., a global leader in advanced chemical formulations.

The company manufactures both positive and negative photoresists, including g-line and advanced immersion formulations capable of forming features at the tens-of-nanometers scale. Its Hillsboro campus comprises several buildings where it produces a wide variety of liquid and powder chemistries. Beyond its own product lines, TOK America provides toll manufacturing, scaling from pilot batches to full commercial volumes, and supports customers with laboratory research, process development, equipment reconfiguration, and a full suite of inspection and analytical services. The inspection laboratory houses instruments such as ICP-MS, ICP-OES, gas and ion chromatographs, a Hitachi SEM, and a Nikon stepper.

Primary customers are semiconductor device makers and packaging houses in the U.S. and Europe, along with medical-device manufacturers. The firm also supplies auxiliary chemicals for semiconductor processing. All projects are conducted under confidentiality agreements, and the company emphasizes its 20-year U.S. manufacturing track record and strict health-and-safety programs for handling hazardous reagents.

TOK America differentiates itself through its ISO 14001-certified environmental management system (registered in 2004), its ability to handle highly corrosive, reactive, and carcinogenic materials safely, and its integrated service model that combines product engineering, packaging, labeling, warehousing, and logistics under one roof.

about:
Twin Marquis Inc. operates from Brooklyn, New York, where it was founded in 1989. The company began in a small New York factory with the goal of producing fresh, high-quality noodles and wrappers for Chinese consumers in the United States who missed home-cooked flavors.

The company manufactures fresh Asian noodles, wrappers, and frozen dumplings, including fully cooked varieties. Its Brooklyn facility processes 15,000 tons of flour each month, and annual noodle production is said to be enough to circle the Earth 100 times. Twin Marquis also offers custom noodle formulations and private-label manufacturing for wholesale partners.

Products are sold through wholesale channels and Asian supermarkets, serving the Chinese American community and broader markets seeking authentic Asian foods. The company's customer base includes wholesale distributors and retail grocery chains specializing in Asian cuisine.

Twin Marquis differentiates itself by being the first Asian-food manufacturer in the U.S. to achieve FSSC 22000 certification from NQA. Dozens of its products carry Kosher and Vegan certifications, and all are produced in a USDA-inspected facility. The company emphasizes food safety and the ability to customize products for wholesale clients.

about:
UEC Advanced Electronics operates from a 64,000-square-foot campus in Hanahan, South Carolina, within the Charleston region. The company was founded in 1995 as UEC Electronics, LLC (Ufkes Engineering and Consulting) by engineers Rebecca and Phil Ufkes, initially developing automation solutions for U.S. government vehicles and power-related products. Recognized as a small, woman-owned business in South Carolina, it became a subsidiary of Albion River LLC in 2025 after a series of acquisitions including Arotech Corporation (2014) and Greenbriar Equity Group (2019).

The company provides end-to-end product design and manufacturing for power storage, generation, and distribution systems. Its capabilities span engineering design, rapid prototyping, precision manufacturing, higher-level assembly, cable and harness assemblies, electromechanical assemblies, circuit card assemblies, and fully integrated multi-rack systems. Core products include mobile power distribution and management systems (MPDMS), modular high-voltage battery packs, intelligent battery systems, vehicle power systems, clean energy generation solutions, and power distribution units. The campus houses engineering, integration, production, and testing operations under one roof.

UEC serves mission-critical markets across defense, aerospace, medical, and industrial sectors. Its battery systems are engineered for aerospace, military, automotive, and renewable energy applications, while the MPDMS platform supports military operations and event management. The company also supports U.S. government vehicle programs and has participated in a Department of Defense mentoring program with Raytheon.

UEC differentiates itself through a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, ISO 13485:2016, and AS9100D, with ITAR registration and RoHS-compliant production lines. Its vision targets global leadership in mission-critical manufacturing, emphasizing agility, quality, technological excellence, and cost efficiency, backed by comprehensive testing, traceability, and continuous improvement.

US Med-Equip is headquartered in Charleston, West Virginia. The company operates as a national provider of medical equipment rentals, sales, and biomedical services to hospitals and health systems.

The company maintains a fleet of over 160,000 pieces of equipment across more than 100 locations nationwide. Its services include movable medical equipment rentals and sales, beds and therapeutic surfaces, biomedical preventive maintenance and repair, asset management, system shutdown support, and telemetry monitoring. Manufacturer-certified biomedical technicians service all equipment, and the company offers free delivery on rentals with a target of two hours plus drive time.

US Med-Equip serves hospitals and health systems across the United States. The company's stated mission is to promote the healing process by providing smart solutions for healthcare partners and patients. It differentiates itself through its GoUSME Connect™ technology platform, which enables clinicians to secure equipment on demand, and a service model that treats every order as if it were for a family member.

Clients include corporations, small businesses, schools, colleges, booster clubs, sports leagues, and individuals. In January 2019, Benson sold the company to Matt Fryman and Marty Choyeske, who continue to run the retail and installation operation.

The shop specializes in off-road parts and accessories for trucks, Jeeps, and SUVs, carrying lines such as BDS Suspension with its “No Fine Print Warranty.” Beyond retail sales, the team provides full vehicle customization and installation services, including lift kits, wheels, tires, and fleet upfitting. Customers range from individual off-road enthusiasts to commercial fleets needing accessory packages.

The company emphasizes a consultative approach: staff guide buyers toward products that match both looks and functionality rather than pushing sales. Its longevity and authorized-dealer status for brands like BDS Suspension are presented as markers of reliability in the local market.

name: Ultralife Corporation
old_description: Designs and manufactures lithium batteries and energy/communications systems
about:
Ultralife Corporation is headquartered in Newark, New York, where it operates a 280,000-square-foot manufacturing and office facility. The company is publicly traded on NASDAQ under the ticker ULBI. While its exact founding year is not disclosed in public materials, Ultralife has grown through strategic acquisitions, integrating brands such as Accutronics, Electrochem Solutions, Excell Battery, and Southwest Electronic Energy Group into a single global operation.

The company designs and manufactures lithium-based batteries, battery packs, chargers, and RF power systems for mission-critical applications. Its production capabilities span high-volume lithium-ion and thionyl chloride cell manufacturing at sites in Newark, Raynham (Massachusetts), and Shenzhen (China), as well as low- to high-volume pack assembly in Houston, the UK, Canada, and India. Ultralife offers more than 350 standard products and provides custom engineering, ruggedization, and lifecycle support lasting 10–15 years in the field.

Ultralife serves government and defense agencies, medical OEMs, industrial and oil-and-gas operators, and commercial customers. Its systems power ruggedized edge servers for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, hot-swappable medical cart batteries, downhole drilling monitors, autonomous underwater vehicles, surgical robots, and measurement-while-drilling tools. The customer base includes hundreds of global OEMs and defense contractors.

Ultralife differentiates itself by focusing on applications where commodity solutions fail, offering deep technical integration with customer design teams, a global footprint with manufacturing redundancy, and ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 certified quality systems. Financial stability as a NASDAQ-listed company and a transparent new-product-development workflow further support its position as a Tier 1 supplier.

name: Unique Custom Furniture
old_description: Each detail in our furniture has been lovingly handcrafted by our master artisans in Fredericktown, Ohio since 1995.
about:
Unique Custom Furniture is based in Fredericktown, Ohio, in Knox County. Founded in 1995 as a family-owned business, the company began when its owners started collecting barnwood from old barns in the surrounding area, refining and finishing the wood, and selling pieces at furniture shows.

The company designs and builds custom furniture from reclaimed chestnut and oak barnwood aged 100–200 years, sourced from Ohio, Appalachia, North Carolina, and Tennessee. The process involves kiln drying for two to four weeks, processing by an Amish wood specialist (planing, straight-line cutting, nail and dust removal), then in-house cutting, sanding, finishing, assembly, and quality inspection. Products include benches, buffets, tables, stools, dressers, hutches, office furniture, and media consoles.

The company’s reclaimed barnwood furniture appeals to buyers seeking heirloom-quality pieces with historical character.

The founders were amazed at the beauty of finished old barnwood long before a barnwood furniture industry existed. They emphasize a unique aesthetic, a refined making process, and the use of genuine American barnwood handcrafted by skilled artisans, positioning each piece as a connection to American history.

United Plastic Molders, Inc. was founded in 1978 in Jackson, Mississippi, by William C. (Bill) Hoge, who remains the principal and actively oversees daily operations. The company began with six employees and four machines and has since expanded to six buildings encompassing more than 60,000 square feet.

A staff of about 60 includes six expert tool and die makers, three molding technicians, and a maintenance director skilled in machine programming. Services cover injection molding, mold design and building, mold repair and inspection, prototyping, CNC machining, UV flatbed printing, and assembly and packaging.

Customers span a range of sectors, with client references including Black & Decker, Tyson Foods, Hobie Cat, Duck Commander, Peavey, and Porter Cable, among others. The company works with both large corporations and individual inventors, providing start-to-finish production from concept to packaged parts.

UPM emphasizes hands-on oversight by its founder, an in-house tooling team with decades of experience, and the flexibility to retrofit facility space, equipment, and storage to meet specific customer requirements. The business has grown largely through word-of-mouth referrals, highlighting a reputation for quality workmanship at competitive prices and on-time delivery.

name: United Semiconductors LLC
old_description: Producer and supplier of binary and ternary III-V semiconductors since 2005.
about:
United Semiconductors LLC was founded in 2005 in Los Alamitos, California. The company operates as a producer and supplier of binary and ternary III‑V semiconductor substrates.

The company specializes in bulk crystal growth of III‑V compounds, delivering polished, double‑sided wafers with diameters from 25 mm to 150 mm (1–6 in) and thicknesses of 0.5–10 mm. Its services span proprietary crystal growth, damage‑free wafer slicing and dicing (up to 75 mm), chemical‑mechanical grinding and polishing, high‑temperature impurity diffusion, activation and annealing (up to 1800 °C), and wet chemical etching, cleaning and passivation. It also produces research‑scale custom materials, nano‑inks (10–500 nm nanocrystals), luminescent powders, and optical components such as prisms and cubes.

United Semiconductors serves the microelectronics, optoelectronics, AI, space, and research sectors. Customers include researchers requiring small‑quantity custom synthesis, foundry partners for the company’s Optoelectronic AI Semiconductor Integrated Solutions (OASIS) Foundry, and organizations seeking space‑grown semiconductor crystals for radiation‑hardened devices.

The company emphasizes its proprietary crystal growth method, which yields uniform composition and high optical transmission with low defect density. It also highlights microgravity‑grown crystals for defect engineering and radiation hardening, and a damage‑free slicing process for both fragile and extremely hard materials.

Universal Packaging is headquartered in Duncan, South Carolina, and traces its roots to 1975 when John Houser and Charlie Muse left Owens Illinois to start Piedmont Packaging, a corrugated sheet plant in Spartanburg. In 1996 the pair launched Universal Packaging as a distribution-focused business from a 21,000‑square‑foot warehouse in Duncan. The company remains privately owned and today operates two facilities in Spartanburg County totaling 170,000 square feet.

The firm’s core business is corrugated packaging, but it also supplies poly film and bags, industrial foam, custom wood crates and pallets, protective non‑woven materials and bags, and provides assembly and kitting services. In‑house capabilities include CAD‑driven packaging design and sampling, ISTA testing, packaging review and performance assessment, and a 170,000‑square‑foot warehousing and inventory management operation supported by a company‑owned delivery fleet.

Universal Packaging serves a diverse customer base across the Carolinas.

The company was founded on a “Spirit of Cooperation” that emphasizes caring for employees and delivering “Relentless Service” to customers.

about:
Uptime Power Systems operates from Warren, Rhode Island, serving New England and the Mid-Atlantic as a manufacturer's representative for emergency power equipment.

The company represents a portfolio of manufacturers including Schneider Electric, Starline, SAI Advanced Power Solutions, BTECH, Trystar, PQ Protection, Bender, HITEC, PermAlert, REON, and Olsun Electrics. Its service scope spans design consultation, equipment selection, layout, project management, load-bank testing, infrared scanning, and commissioning support for UPS systems, switchgear, power distribution units, busway, cooling, battery monitoring, and prefabricated data-center modules. A seven-person team — including a licensed professional engineer and former Eaton application engineers — delivers technical support from specification through startup.

Uptime's customers operate in data centers, healthcare and medical imaging, industrial plants, utilities, institutional and public facilities, transit systems, water and wastewater treatment, and life-sciences laboratories. The firm works directly with consulting engineers, contractors, and facilities teams that require reliable backup power in environments where downtime carries significant risk.

Uptime positions itself as a single point of accountability for the entire power chain, emphasizing that it remains engaged after the purchase order through commissioning and ongoing support. about:
Founded in 2015 in Murfreesboro, Tennessee, Urban Timber Supply began by crafting custom furniture from locally salvaged hardwood, often sourced from trees that have been part of a family's history for generations. The company transforms these logs into pieces intended to last for generations to come.

The workshop produces a range of custom wood furniture, from small handcrafted items such as executive pens to 15-foot conference tables. Using live-edge slabs of walnut, maple, ash, poplar, cherry, and oak, the team mills, finishes, and occasionally incorporates epoxy resin to accentuate the natural character of each piece. An inventory of hand-selected slabs — black walnut up to 15 feet long and maple up to 15 feet long — is kept on hand for immediate projects.

Urban Timber Supply serves both residential and commercial clients. Homeowners commission dining tables, benches, and statement pieces like a black walnut pool table built into a beachfront home. Commercial projects include office builds and conference tables, notably a custom table installed in the historic Murfreesboro Courthouse.

The company emphasizes preserving the story embedded in the wood. Its approach centers on well-sourced material, careful craftsmanship, and designs meant to feel personal, substantial, and lasting — turning a client's own tree into a functional heirloom.

VR Industries, Inc. was founded in 1985 in Warwick, Rhode Island. The company has operated as an electronic contract manufacturer for nearly four decades, building a legacy of producing printed circuit board assemblies and electromechanical systems for a range of regulated industries.

Medical customers include top global OEMs receiving moderate to complex PCBAs and full system assemblies. Defense work extends to every branch of the armed forces, supported by a workforce that includes veterans. Industrial clients receive custom electronic and mechanical assemblies built to ISO 9001, ISO 13485, FDA, and MIL-spec requirements.

The company emphasizes a partnership-driven model that prioritizes close collaboration from concept through delivery. Its differentiators include in-house IPC-certified trainers, a franchised-distributor supply chain strategy, and certifications covering ISO 9001, ISO 13485, ITAR, UL 508A, FDA registration, RoHS, and GIDEP.

name: VSL Packaging Company USA
old_description: Our goal at VSL Packaging is to be a one stop shop for packaging products and a leading provider of innovative retail, e-commerce, and custom corrugated packaging.
about:
VSL Packaging operates from a design office and showroom at 239 West 29th Street in Manhattan's Garment District. The company began in 2009 as the packaging arm of Varick Street Litho (VSL Print), a Manhattan commercial printer that has appeared on CNBC's The Profit. VSL Packaging launched its own dedicated website in 2020, but the operation shares the West 29th Street address and the print craft heritage of its parent company.

The company designs, prototypes, and manufactures custom packaging — rigid boxes, folding cartons, corrugated boxes, retail bags, point-of-purchase displays, corrugated shippers, and luxury mailers — all produced in New York City. The process moves through structural design, photorealistic 3D rendering, physical prototyping, dieline creation, and pre-production proofs before printing and finishing. Finishing options include embossing, debossing, foil stamping, spot UV, matte, gloss, satin, and soft-touch lamination. VSL also provides shipping and fulfillment services such as kitting, assembly, warehousing, pick-pack-ship, and freight coordination. The company reports more than 10,000 packaging projects completed across 16 box styles.

VSL serves roughly two dozen industries, including apparel, beauty, beverages, CBD, cosmetics, electronics, food, jewelry, luxury goods, medical, pharmaceuticals, and sporting goods. Its customer base ranges from early-stage startups to national brands; documented projects include packaging for Belvedere Vodka, Google, IBM, Betty Booze, Bored Cow, and Charlie Fox.

VSL differentiates itself by controlling the entire production chain under one roof: the design desk, prototyping bench, press schedule, and finishing work all reside at the same Manhattan address. The company emphasizes that it owns the job it sells, avoiding brokers and overseas factories. Quote follow-up occurs within one business day, and minimum order quantities are kept low and flexible, quoted per project.

name: VTi by M. Davis Power Distribution Equipment (owned by M. Davis & Sons, Inc.)
old_description: M. Davis & Sons manufactures and supplies low voltage industrial electrical power distribution equipment for industry partners, through the VTi by M. Davis division.
about:
VTi by M. Davis Power Distribution Equipment operates from Newark, Delaware, as a division of M. Davis & Sons, Inc. The company manufactures and supplies low-voltage industrial electrical power distribution equipment for industry partners.

The VTi division combines engineering, fabrication, and testing to produce a range of UL-listed, U.S.-made power distribution products. Its lineup includes Unitized Distribution Systems (UDS), Dual Voltage UDS (dv-UDS), Portable Power Distribution Centers (PPDC), and Fused Distribution Panels (FDP) in both AC and DC versions. The company operates a panel shop where units are assembled, tested, and shipped ready for installation, and also offers panel refurbishing services that bring outdated equipment up to current UL-certified standards.

Customers include engineering firms, industrial plants, facilities, and construction projects that need temporary or permanent power distribution. The equipment serves in-plant applications, critical process protection, and temporary power for construction sites. The dv-UDS is designed for dual-voltage requirements, while the PPDC addresses fast-turnaround portable power needs.

The company positions itself as a turnkey "One Source for All" industrial construction services provider, delivering end-to-end custom solutions from layout through field installation and startup. It highlights a 20% cost savings factor for UDS units compared to separately mounted enclosures, and emphasizes full customization, UL listing, and domestic manufacturing as key differentiators.
